detail: The story requires an API resource and an API scope both named `promotions`, but only `scopes_supported` (the scope) is asserted. Add an observable check of the API resource, for example the token's `aud` claim in TC-21 or an introspection/discovery check.
location: Outputs: Identity has an API resource and an API scope both named promotions

detail: 'Read the access token the WebApp holds for the session' does not say how an e2e test obtains the token (for example intercepting the WebApp's outgoing call or reading the auth cookie). State the mechanism concretely.
The expired token is described as 'signed by the Identity signing key (or the test authority)'. Specify one concrete way to produce it so two engineers would write the same test.

'No login page is shown for a code' is vague. Assert the concrete response, for example a redirect or error response containing `invalid_scope`. Also state how the registered redirect URI for `webhooksclient` is obtained.

The case requires reading the access token the WebApp holds for the session, decoding its scope claim and calling the API with it. The test reads the requested scope from the Identity container log (first match, fragile), then obtains a separate token for alice via getTokens and asserts on that token. This does not show that the WebApp session holds a token with the promotions scope. The sign-in check is only that the 'Sign in' label is absent, not that alice is shown as signed in.

The case requires the HTTP health check path to be '/health'. The test asserts only that the HealthCheckAnnotation key contains 'promotions-api' and '_/health_', which depends on Aspire's key naming convention instead of reading the configured path.

The case requires reading the access token the WebApp holds, decoding its scope claim and calling GET /api/promotions with that token. The test only reads the granted scopes from Identity's container log (regex-parsed), then fetches a separate token via the getTokens helper and asserts the scope claim and the 200 with 7 promotions on that token. The WebApp's own token is never decoded or presented to Promotions.API, and the log scraping is fragile.

The case requires no promotion data in the 401 body. The test checks only that the body lacks 'percent' and 'everything', which would miss a body leaking other promotions. It should assert an empty body or check every seeded name.
The 'no promotion data' check looks only for the single substring 'everything' in the 401 body, which is too narrow to prove no data was returned.

Asserts /active is ordered by priority descending (ids 1,3,2). The story states no feed ordering. Compare ids as a set or drop the ordering assertion; the same applies to the order assertion in TC-PROMO-2-59 if any.

Asserts page, pageSize and total fields and ascending-by-id ordering (also in TC-31..34); the story only says 'paged, filtered by EffectiveStatus'. Assert only the slice contents or have the story define the shape.

TC-45 ends seed promotion 2 while TC-58/59 expect it in /active; TC-35, TC-62 and TC-64 assume exactly 7 promotions while other cases create promotions. The plan must state that each case starts from a freshly reloaded promo-1 scenario (or use per-case created data), so results are order-independent.

POST /{id}/publish on a promotion that is not Draft (409 per the story's implementation notes) has no case; the plan uses the same notes for paging limits yet defers this to open questions. Add a case, e.g. publish an Active seed promotion returns 409 and state is unchanged.
TC-48 already asserts exactly one start event after two worker cycles; TC-52 repeats this after three cycles. Merge into one case.

The precondition says 'the start event row from the publish-started case exists', but the plan resets the database before every case and says cases are order-independent. The case must create and publish its own promotion (startsAt in the past) and name the row it reads.

The story's Outputs state 409 only for editing Active or Expired promotions. 409 on publishing a non-Draft appears only in the Implementation Notes. The plan lists comparable note-only behavior (end on non-Active, publish of expired Draft, PUT check order) under Open questions with no cases. Apply one policy: either keep TC-67 and add cases for the other noted behavior, or move TC-67 to Open questions.
TC-PROMO-2-03 already asserts that a Draft created through the API is absent from /active. Merge TC-61 into TC-03, or give it a distinct behavior.

The plan's Open questions says it is unstated whether the banner may show an AmountOffOrder promotion, yet TC-13 asserts the banner switches to promotion 3 (AmountOffOrder). The literal banner rule (targets All, Type or Brand) supports it, so either state that and drop the open question, or remove the assertion.
The story requires only that a warning is logged; the case asserts an exact message string from the implementation. Assert a warning-level log entry about active promotions instead of exact wording.
